points.description: States that a pointer is a variable (not merely an address, value or data type) that stores/holds/contains a memory address.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if it says it stores an address but does not clearly call it a variable (or calls it a variable but is vague about what it holds).

points.description: States that the address held is the memory location of another variable (i.e. the pointer refers to/points to another variable's location in memory).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if it says it holds a memory address but does not say it is of another variable/object.

points.description: Correctly distinguishes a pointer from an ordinary variable: a pointer holds an address (indirect access to another variable), whereas an ordinary variable holds the data value itself.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a precise statement that a pointer is a variable holding the memory address of another variable, using terms like "variable", "address" and "memory". Part marks only where clearly more than half of a point is precise, as stated in partial_credit. Vague answers such as "it points to something", "it is a reference" or "it is a data type", or any wrong statement (e.g. a pointer stores the value of another variable), earn nothing for that point.
